The catalyst of step (i), named in [0031], [0033], [0035], [0038] and [0039]. One record merged from four forms this section prints for one compound: 'ruthenium (IV) oxide' three times, 'RuO2' eight times, and 'ruthenium oxide' and 'ruthenium dioxide' once each in [0033]. The identifier is the form the Claims and the Examples also print, so the record joins theirs, and the oxidation-state form is kept as an alias so the (IV) reading is not lost. [0033] says it is recovered as an insoluble solid in substantially the same amount as initially and can be filtered off and reused without treatment; the same sentence prints '(for >50 conversion)' with no unit and no percent sign, which is kept as printed and not interpreted. The phrase 'the ruthenium catalyst' in [0033] and [0034] covers this oxide, its hydrate and the trichloride together and names no one compound, so it is not recorded. Ruthenium dioxide hydrate and ruthenium trichloride are separate records.

[0032] offers it as an example of the oxidizing agent for step (i). The alkali metal is not specified, so the string names a family of salts rather than one compound and resolved is false; it is not merged into the sodium hypochlorite record, which [0035] names separately, and it is not narrowed to sodium here. 'the hypochlorite' in [0033] refers back to this phrase and is kept as an alias. The bare class word 'peroxide' in the same sentence names no compound and is not recorded; hydrogen peroxide, the example the text gives for it, is. [0031], [0038] and [0039] say only 'an oxidant', and the arrows of the scheme spans at lines 181, 205 and 222 print only 'Oxidant'; neither names a compound and neither produces a record.

[0032] names it as the peroxide example of the oxidizing agent for step (i). Prose only: no scheme span in this section draws or names a peroxide, and no quantity, temperature or time is attached to it. The generic head of the phrase, 'peroxide', is not recorded separately.

[0033] names it as one of the three species formed when the ruthenium catalyst is oxidized by the hypochlorite, and says the oxidation preferably goes to the ruthenate. Printed as an anion with no counter cation, so it does not identify one compound and resolved is false. Role recorded as catalyst because the text presents it as the oxidized form of the catalyst; the section does not say which of the three species does the oxidising, so it is not recorded as an oxidant.

[0033] names it as the third species formed when the ruthenium catalyst is oxidized by the hypochlorite. Resolved: unlike the ruthenate and perruthenate anions of the same sentence, the tetroxide names one neutral compound. Role recorded as catalyst because the text presents it as an oxidized form of the catalyst, not as an added oxidant; the section says the oxidation preferably stops at the ruthenate rather than going to it.

[0033] says the ruthenium can be supplied as ruthenium dioxide or as ruthenium dioxide hydrate, and that the hydrate is the preferred form. Kept as a record of its own rather than as an alias of the ruthenium oxide record, because a hydrate is a different substance; the water content is not stated. 'ruthenium dioxide' in the same sentence is the anhydrous oxide and is an alias of that other record.

[0034] offers it as the salt form of the ruthenium catalyst and says the catalyst RuO2 can be formed in situ in a reaction commencing with it. The sentence runs across the p10 to p11 page break and its continuation at line 192 carries no paragraph marker. 'an aqueous caustic solution' in that continuation names no specific base and is not recorded as a compound.
